description: A whole-degree tour of what a computer is, how information is represented and moved, and what computing does to society, so that every later course has a map to hang on. Taught to the depth of a leading introductory computer science survey, with hands-on exercises for every idea.
modelledOn: Brookshear and Brylow, Computer Science: An Overview
Schneider and Gersting, Invitation to Computer Science
Petzold, Code: The Hidden Language of Computer Hardware and Software
outcomes: Describe the parts of a computer and trace how a program and its data move from storage to processor and back.
Represent text, numbers, images and sound in binary and estimate storage and bandwidth needs.
Explain what algorithms, programs, operating systems and compilers are and how they fit together.
Organise information in files, spreadsheets and relational databases and query it.
Explain how the Internet and the Web work end to end, from a URL to a rendered page.
Reason about safety, privacy, ethics and the social impact of computing with Ghanaian and global examples.

units.title: What computing is
topics: History of computing: from the abacus and Babbage to the transistor, the microprocessor and the smartphone
Computational thinking: decomposition, abstraction, patterns, algorithms
Hardware, software, data and people as the parts of a computing system
Kinds of computers: embedded, mobile, personal, server, supercomputer, cloud

units.title: Representing information
topics: Bits and bytes; binary, hexadecimal; units from kilobyte to petabyte
Integers and two's complement; floating point and why 0.1 + 0.2 is not 0.3
Text: ASCII, Unicode and UTF-8; representing Twi and other Ghanaian languages
Images (pixels, colour depth, compression), sound (sampling, bit depth) and video
Compression: run-length, Huffman and the difference between lossless and lossy
Error detection: parity and checksums

units.title: Inside the computer
topics: Logic gates and how they add; the processor, registers, clock and the fetch-decode-execute cycle
Memory hierarchy: registers, cache, RAM, SSD, hard disk, cloud storage
Input and output devices, buses and ports
Machine code, assembly, high-level languages, compilers and interpreters
Operating systems: what they do for programs and users; processes and files

units.title: Algorithms and programs
topics: Algorithms as precise procedures; pseudocode and flowcharts
Sequence, selection and iteration; variables and data types
Searching and sorting by hand: linear search, binary search, bubble and selection sort
Why some algorithms are faster: counting steps, growth with input size
Writing and running short programs in Scratch and Python to see the ideas work
Software: system software, application software, open source, licences

units.title: Information management, files and databases
topics: Data, information and knowledge; data quality and data life cycle
File systems, folders, file formats, metadata; backup and archiving
Spreadsheets for data: formulas, sorting, filtering, charts
Relational databases: tables, keys, relationships; simple SQL SELECT queries
Database applications: student records, mobile money ledgers, hospital systems
Big data and data centres: what changes at scale

units.title: Computer networks, the Internet and the Web
topics: LANs, WANs, Wi-Fi, mobile data; switches and routers
IP addresses, DNS, packets and the layered model in plain terms
What happens when you type a URL: HTTP, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, servers and browsers
Email, cloud services, content delivery and why pages load slowly on poor links
Submarine cables and Ghana's connectivity; data costs and digital inclusion
Building a one-page website

units.title: Computer safety, security and ethics
topics: Threats: malware, phishing, mobile money scams, social engineering
Passwords, two-factor authentication, encryption and HTTPS in plain terms
Personal data, privacy and Ghana's Data Protection Act
Professional ethics and the ACM Code; plagiarism and academic integrity
Safe and healthy computer use

units.title: Technology and society
topics: Computing in Ghana and Africa: mobile money, agritech, e-government, health informatics
Automation, AI and the future of work; the digital divide
Environmental cost of computing: energy, e-waste at Agbogbloshie
Careers and the map of the computer science degree ahead
